The old city of Konigsberg had four landmasses connected by seven bridges, arranged so that every single landmass was touched by an odd number of bridges. Euler proved it is impossible to walk through the city crossing each bridge exactly once. Why not?
choices: Because seven is an odd number of bridges
A route crossing every bridge exactly once can exist only if zero or exactly two landmasses have an odd number of bridges touching them - but here all four do
Because the landmasses are not arranged in a straight line
Because there are more bridges than landmasses

questions.q: Dice A, B, and C are weighted so that A beats B more often than not in a single roll-off, and B beats C more often than not. Must A also beat C more often than not?
choices: No - nontransitive dice can be constructed where A beats B, B beats C, and yet C beats A
Yes, but only if all three dice are six-sided
No, because probabilities can never exceed 50%
Yes, this follows automatically from transitivity

questions.q: Cantor's diagonal argument proves that no list, however long, can ever contain every real number between 0 and 1 - even though the list of natural numbers (1, 2, 3, ...) is already infinite. What does this establish?
choices: The real numbers between 0 and 1 and the natural numbers are the same size of infinity
There are more natural numbers than real numbers between 0 and 1
Infinity is not a well-defined mathematical concept
The real numbers between 0 and 1 form a strictly larger infinity than the natural numbers

questions.q: A factory's widgets come from two machines: Machine A makes 70% of all widgets with a 2% defect rate; Machine B makes 30% of all widgets with a 5% defect rate. A widget is picked at random and found to be defective. Is it more likely to have come from Machine A or Machine B?
choices: There's not enough information to tell
Machine A, since it produces most of the widgets
Machine B - despite making fewer widgets overall, its higher defect rate means about 51.7% of defective widgets come from it

Gabriel's Horn is formed by rotating the curve y = 1/x for x ≥ 1 around the x-axis. It has a finite volume (π cubic units) when computed by integration. What is its total surface area?
choices: Zero, since the horn narrows to an infinitely thin point
Finite, and larger than the volume
Exactly π, same as the volume
Infinite — the surface area diverges even though the volume is finite

questions.q: For any ranked-choice voting system with 3 or more candidates, is it possible to design one that always satisfies all three of: no single dictator, respects unanimous voter preference, and is unaffected by irrelevant candidates being added or removed?
choices: Yes, but only when there are exactly 3 candidates
No — Arrow's Impossibility Theorem proves no such ranked voting system can satisfy all three simultaneously
Yes, instant-runoff voting satisfies all three
Yes, ranked-pairs voting satisfies all three
